title: Chapter 99
content:
"Come on. Suck it clean, and maybe I'll give you an answer."

Jakyeong bared his teeth, letting out a razor-sharp, chilling laugh.

"Sure. Step a little closer. I'll rip the meat off with my teeth and chew it to bone."

"Insolent little shit."

THUD.

Before the sentence fully landed, the guard’s steel-toed boot slammed straight into Jakyeong's ribs, followed by a heavy right cross.

"Hey, easy! Stop!" the other guard called out, but the rage had already taken over.

Tied securely to the wooden chair, Jakyeong toppled sideways, hitting the concrete with a dull crack as a barrage of kicks rained down on his torso. The second guard finally hauled the attacker off, hauling the chair upright.

Jakyeong tilted his head, spitting a dark clump of blood onto the floorboards with a wet ptoo.

His wrists and ankles were bound in layers of industrial hemp; slipping the knots with raw friction was out of the question. Has the signal reached Han-ge yet? How long until Park Tae-soo mobilizes? Every passing second felt like a noose tightening around his neck.

As he masked his rising panic, heavy, dragging footsteps echoed from the exposed exterior corridor. Both sentries snapped to attention.

Jakyeong turned his head, his dark eyes blowing wide.

"Still full of fight, are we? Even wrapped up like a pig for slaughter."

The cold, rasping voice belonged unmistakably to Takeya Jun.

A thick white bandage covered his gouged right eye socket, his shattered forearm secured in a rigid splint. In his uninjured hand, he casually flipped a tactical combat knife, catching the hilt by the balance point with practiced ease.

The two guards backed off with deferential nods. Jun crossed the floor, sinking into a crouch directly in front of the chair to study Jakyeong’s swollen, battered face.

"Look at you. Taken down without breaking a sweat. Pathetic."

Jakyeong dragged his gaze across the mangled hitman, his lips pulling into a faint, mocking sneer.

"You're hardly in any position to talk, aniki. Can you even see out of that side of your skull?"

Jun’s expression went dead. He brought the razor-sharp tip of the blade to rest a millimeter below Jakyeong's right lower eyelid. The slightest twitch would burst the globe like a grape. Slowly, he dragged the steel down the boy's cheek, trailing a fine, stinging line of red before resting the edge against his carotid artery.

"How should I end this, Wei? A clean slice across the throat? Or should I butcher you into neat little parcels and courier the meat to your beloved brothers?"

When Jakyeong offered only cold silence, Jun clamped his calloused hand around the boy's jaw, digging his thumb deep into the bone.

"Answer me. Well?"

"Do whatever the fuck you want, you one-eyed bastard!"

Jun’s face twisted into sudden, psychotic fury. He delivered a brutal front kick that launched the chair backward. Standing over the fallen frame, he drove the blade deep into Jakyeong’s unhealed bicep, dragging the steel through the torn muscle before repeating the exact same butcher's stroke on the other arm.

"AAARGH—!"

A raw, agonized scream ripped through the concrete cavern, echoing out into the empty sky.

Drip. Drip.

A steady stream of crimson dripped from the bridge of Il-hyun's nose, pooling on the dusty floorboards.

His wrists were cinched raw behind his spine. Shattered, splintered timber from broken construction studs littered the concrete around his knees. Half a dozen enforcers armed with heavy iron pipes and two-by-fours formed a tight perimeter, while Chairman Kang sat quietly in an armchair directly opposite, watching his battered son with the detached indifference of a butcher inspecting a carcass.

"There is an old proverb," the Chairman mused, tapping his brass-tipped cane against the floor. "A rabid dog understands only the stick."

Spitting a mouthful of dark, clotted blood, Il-hyun let out a low, breathless scoff.

"There's another classic, Father. Once a dog grows old and toothless... it belongs in the dirt."

"A pity. It seems you still fail to grasp the reality of your board."

The Chairman made a faint flick of his wrist.

An enforcer stepped forward, driving a heavy two-by-four across Il-hyun's shoulder blades. The concussive blow forced the breath from his lungs with a wet gasp, driving his knees hard into the concrete.

As Il-hyun glared up with pure, homicidal malice, Chief Secretary Kim approached, setting a blank sheet of heavy stock paper and a luxury fountain pen on the floor before stepping back.

"Transcribe what I dictate," the Chairman commanded.

"Go fuck yourself, Father."

"Your suicide note."

Staring down at the pristine white page, Il-hyun broke into a dry, breathless laugh. He ran his tongue along his shredded inner cheek, spitting another glob of red across the paper.

"Fuck... If you have the nerve to put me down, just pull the trigger yourself."

"Write," the patriarch continued, entirely unbothered. "'I, Kang Il-hyun, having succumbed to a severe worsening of long-standing psychiatric instability—'"

Ha. Il-hyun threw his head back, laughing with incredulous mirth before his expression hardened into an arctic mask.

"Was my insanity truly that transparent?"

The Chairman didn't miss a beat. "'—wishing to cause no further distress or liability to my family and associates, hereby surrender all corporate claims, equity, and inheritance, and choose to end my life by my own hand.'"

Il-hyun’s lips curved into a wicked, bloody smirk.

"Postscript: The architect of this homicide is Chairman Kang Hoon."

CRACK. THUD.

Two successive strikes from the iron pipe drove into Il-hyun's ribs, snapping bone.

Losing his patience, the Chairman surged to his feet, stepping into point-blank range and bringing the heavy brass head of his walking cane down across Il-hyun’s face.

SMACK. CRACK.

The brutal impacts fractured the cheekbone, sending a deafening, high-pitched ringing tearing through Il-hyun's right ear. Split flesh burst open, painting his collar in fresh, hot crimson.

Il-hyun lifted his chin, his dark eyes wide and manic, staring directly into the patriarch's face as he let out a broken, unhinged laugh.

Watching the feral, unrepentant beast before him, the Chairman’s gray pupils darkened into an icy abyss. Even in chains, the boy was terrifying; even as his own flesh and blood, he was a monster that needed to be put down.

No one laid claim to his empire without permission. No one took what was his. Blood relation conferred zero immunity.

"I should have crushed your skull the day you were born," the Chairman whispered, his voice dropping into gravel. "When your mother threatened to swallow rat poison, I should have let the whore die with you in her belly."

Il-hyun met the stare, enunciating every syllable with chilling precision:

"You certainly should have."

Just then, a sharp, agonized cry tore through the unfinished concrete partition from the adjacent bay—Lee Ja-kyeong’s voice.

The madman’s smirk evaporated from Il-hyun's face in an instant, his features draining into a pale, horrified void.

Watching the sudden, devastating crack in his son's armor, a cruel, triumphant smile spread across the Chairman’s withered lips. With the tip of his cane, he shoved the blank suicide note aside.

Il-hyun’s head snapped toward his father, the veins in his neck bulging against his skin.

"What's wrong? Laugh a little more."

"I'll write whatever the fuck you want," Il-hyun rasped, his voice trembling with a lethal, suffocating frost. "Do not lay another finger on him."

Though framed as a concession, the words carried the weight of an executioner's vow.

When the Chairman merely stared back in mocking silence, the last thread of Il-hyun's control snapped completely.

"Fuck you! I said I'd give you whatever you want!"

Watching his son unravel was an entirely novel, fascinating spectacle. For a boy who had spent his life draped in untouchable, aristocratic arrogance, seeing him reduced to such desperate, frantic begging sparked a dark, sadistic thrill in the old man's chest.

"I have lived by a single creed my entire life," the Chairman murmured.

"..."

"'There are those I trust never to betray me. I call them corpses.'"

The air around Il-hyun turned to dry ice. A blinding, suffocating rage clawed up his throat, yet the heavy hemp cords around his wrists refused to yield.

Another muffled shout echoed from the adjacent room, driving the panic behind his ribs to a fever pitch.

The Chairman savored every second of his son's torment. There was no finer instrument to break a disobedient heir than stripping away the one thing he desperately sought to keep.

"Shall we put that conviction to the test today?"

Before Il-hyun could speak, the Chairman gave Secretary Kim a curt hand signal. The secretary vanished into the corridor, and the shouting in the next room abruptly ceased.

Il-hyun looked out through the open wall. A high floor. The Chairman’s playbook was painfully obvious: force the signed confession, then toss his body over the ledge into the street below.

Through the unfinished concrete opening, the afternoon sky was a breathtaking, brilliant azure. A gorgeous, sun-drenched day.

The heavy door creaked open, and Secretary Kim dragged Jakyeong across the threshold.

Trailing right behind was Takeya Jun, twirling his bloody combat knife with a repulsive, one-eyed leer. Jakyeong was barely conscious, fresh dark blood pouring down both shredded forearms to splatter against the floor.

Seeing Il-hyun drenched in blood and kneeling on the concrete, Jakyeong froze in stunned horror.

A suffocating guilt seized his throat. If I hadn't made that stupid, impulsive confession this morning... if he had just stayed at his desk like an ordinary CEO... he wouldn't be bleeding out on this floor.

An enforcer shoved Jakyeong down, forcing him onto his knees beside Il-hyun.

Taking in the boy's mangled arms, Il-hyun locked eyes with his father, his gaze burning with pure, unadulterated hatred.

"I will sign the papers. Release him."

"Release who? You? Or this stray?"

"Release Lee Ja-kyeong."

The Chairman’s eyes shifted to Jakyeong. Had this little assassin executed his contract properly a year ago, none of this mess would exist. He had fully intended to put a bullet through the boy's head, but the prospect of teaching his arrogant son one final, devastating lesson in human betrayal was far too delicious to pass up.

The agony of being gutted by the very hand you cherished.

Chairman Kang nodded.

An enforcer drew a combat blade, slicing the zip-ties from Jakyeong’s wrists.

Before Jakyeong could process the sudden freedom, Secretary Kim drew a heavy woodchopping hatchet from his tactical harness, tossing the steel weapon onto the concrete between them.

The moment Jakyeong’s fingers twitched toward the handle, Kim leveled a suppressed sidearm at his forehead.

"Do not attempt anything foolish."

Jakyeong tore his eyes from the hatchet, looking up at the Chairman.

"My son seems to place an extraordinary amount of faith in you," the old man said, his voice dripping with venomous amusement.

"..."

"What about you, boy? Do you share that same devotion?"

Jakyeong turned his head to look at Il-hyun.

Il-hyun kept his gaze pinned straight ahead, refusing to meet his eyes.

Why? Why aren't you looking at me?

Before the puzzle pieces could settle, Chairman Kang delivered an unthinkable ultimatum:

"Sever his right arm at the shoulder. Do that, and you walk out of this building alive."

Jakyeong’s breath hitched. He snapped his head toward Il-hyun.

The man remained entirely motionless, staring dead into the blank concrete ahead.

Look at me. Look at me, damn it.

"President Kang."

Il-hyun slowly closed his eyes, pretending to hear nothing.

The brutal, calculated reality crashed down on Jakyeong like an avalanche.

Fuck. Fuck.

He ground his teeth, his eyes boring into Chairman Kang with lethal hatred.

The patriarch hadn't kept his son alive out of lingering parental love. Kang Il-hyun’s sadistic habit of playing with his prey before the kill was a direct genetic inheritance. The old monster didn't just want physical death—he wanted to crush his son's soul, forcing him to watch the boy he loved swing the executioner's blade.

Slowly, deliberately, Jakyeong extended his hand, his fingers closing tightly around the hickory handle of the hatchet.

The surrounding mercenaries immediately adjusted their aim, dozens of laser sights converging on his chest, ready to ventilate him the instant the steel deviated from its target.

Jakyeong stood up, the heavy axe resting in his grip.

Kneeling on the concrete, Kang Il-hyun let his chin drop in total, quiet resignation.

Jakyeong understood why the man refused to look at him. He's keeping his eyes shut so I won't hesitate. So we won't both die in a hail of lead.

Sweat mixed with blood, slicking the wooden handle.

"Ha... Fuck my life."

The Chairman leaned forward on his cane, his patience wearing thin. "Must I wait all afternoon?"

Jakyeong called out in a low, steady voice:

"President Kang."

Silence.

Jakyeong parted his lips, the words barely a whisper:

"I'm sorry..."

A microscopic, heartbreaking smile touched the corner of Il-hyun's bruised lips. He knelt motionless, offering his neck like a condemned prisoner awaiting the block.

I'm truly sorry, you lunatic. I'll spend the rest of my miserable life paying for this.

Jakyeong raised the heavy hatchet high above his shoulder.

Pure, ecstatic triumph ignited across Chairman Kang’s wrinkled face.

Staring down at Il-hyun's bowed head, Jakyeong pivoted his entire body in a blinding, explosive three-hundred-and-sixty-degree rotational spin—hurling the hatchet across the room with every ounce of kinetic force in his frame.

The heavy steel axe blurred through the air, completely bypassing the guards' reaction time, and buried its broad blade dead center into Chairman Kang’s forehead with a sickening, concussive THWACK.

Bone splintered. Brain matter sprayed across the drywall.

In the exact same heartbeat, Kang Il-hyun’s eyes snapped wide open.

He watched in absolute, stunned paralysis as his father's body toppled backward out of the armchair, the heavy hatchet wedged deep between his eyes.

Il-hyun slowly turned his head to look up at Jakyeong.

Standing amidst the stunned mercenaries with blood dripping from both arms, Jakyeong offered a tired, painfully apologetic, crooked little smile.

"Sorry. Looks like you're an orphan now."
